subject: Context length profiling & pricing qualification with Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: context length profiling & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion on how Acme AI is using long-context models for multi-doc summarization and developer assistant flows. Quick recap and a few asks that will help us put together an accurate pricing estimate and quantify the right capacity: 

1) Usage profile we discussed (please confirm):
   - Primary apps: Knowledge summarization (batch ingest + query), developer assistant (interactive).
   - Latency SLOs: 200-500ms for interactive, batch can be minutes.

2) Key data points we need for pricing + context-length sizing:
   - Average prompt tokens per request (avg across flows)
   - Average completion tokens per request
   - Percentile breakdown (50/90/95/99) for total context length (prompt + completion)
   - Rough monthly request volume and total tokens (prompts vs completions)
   - What % of requests need >8k tokens, >32k, >128k context?
   - Target unit economics / target $ per 1M tokens (stretch/expected/upper bound)

3) Ops/security notes:
   - Any compliance needs (SOC2, data residency) that should be in the estimate?

I've attached a short template (context_length_profile.xlsx) you can drop numbers into — but a CSV or exported sample logs work too if that's easier.

Next steps: if you can send the numbers by end of day Friday (11/13) Jordan and I will draft a 2-option pricing estimate (batched + baseline and optimized with KV caching / quantization) and propose a follow-up technical review with Vivek.

Thanks — look forward to the numbers.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-13T09:18:00-08:00

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the template. I filled in the high-level numbers below (exported from our usage logs; happy to share raw CSV if you want finer slices).

Summary (monthly):
- Avg prompt tokens per request: 620
- Avg completion tokens per request: 1,450
- Monthly request volume: ~120,000 requests/month
- Monthly prompt tokens: ~74.4M
- Monthly completion tokens: ~174M
- 50th percentile total tokens: 1,900
- 90th percentile total tokens: 6,800
- 95th percentile total tokens: 18,200
- 99th percentile total tokens: 52,000
- % requests needing >8k tokens: ~18%
- % requests needing >32k tokens: ~5%
- % requests needing >128k tokens: ~0.6%

Budget target / unit economics:
- We are currently targeting ~$15-20 per 1M tokens (across prompt+completion) as the ballpark for a first-year committed price to hit our internal ROI. We can be flexible if there are clear ops savings (caching/kv) or a commitment to reserved capacity.

Compliance: We will need SOC2 and a standard DPA; data residency within the US is preferred but not mandatory for the first pilot. Procurement contact is procurement@acme.ai (Jill will loop them in).

Samir

samir.patel@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: context length profiling & next steps

Samir — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the percentile detail — very helpful. A few clarifying q's so our pricing and capacity plan is accurate: 

1) The 95th & 99th percentiles look like they drive the need for 32k/128k variants. For the ~5% at >32k and ~0.6% at >128k, are those single-request sizes (single prompt+completion) or include multi-request aggregation (e.g., multiple docs concatenated pre-query)?
2) For the 18% >8k bucket — is that mostly prompt-heavy (long context passed in) or completion-heavy (long generated summaries)?
3) Any seasonal spikes (monthly peak factor vs average)? If you can share a 7-day rolling peak or a single-day peak factor that would let us size dedicated pool vs burst.

We'll put together two pricing options:
- Option A: baseline hosted pricing with modest discounts at commit levels (costed on total tokens + small fixed per-request fee).
- Option B: optimized plan — reserved capacity for the heavy tail (32k/128k slots), KV-caching suggestions (we can reduce completion tokens for repeated context), and a quantized model variant for the bulk of traffic. This usually reduces per-token cost and keeps interactive latency low.

I've attached an initial estimate PDF (acme_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf) that lays out the math using the numbers you shared — it's conservative and assumes no cache benefit. If you can confirm answers to the questions above (especially whether the >32k and >128k requests are single queries), Vivek can run a quick infra sketch for dedicated vs burst.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sizing on Thursday 11/19 at 10:00am PT with Vivek and Jordan. Does that work?

--
Marissa Cole
